rationale: Start with a broad, mid-temperature scouting gradient to elute all 6 compounds and map the elution window without risking truncation. This gives useful first estimates of whether peaks are unretained, still on the hold, and where the critical pairs sit.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the score is limited only by late elution; now optimize speed aggressively. The first run suggests the actual elution window is much narrower than 0.05–0.95, so use a tighter, steeper window and higher temperature to pull the last peak toward 10 min while checking that resolution stays above 1.5.

We already have the maximum CRF, so this run probes whether the method can be made even faster while staying fully resolved, with the closest pair being peaks 1/2. Raising phi0, shortening tG, and increasing T should move the first peaks later and compress the run; if pair 1/2 remains above 1.5, this defines a leaner robust operating point.

Injection 3 showed the earliest pair is the limiting one; lowering phi0 one step should re-retain and spread peaks 1/2 while keeping the faster 6 min gradient and 55 C. This tests whether we can preserve full resolution with a shorter method than injection 2.

The 6 min method is close, but pair 1/2 is slightly under-resolved at 55 C; lowering temperature should increase retention and often improve that early selectivity with only a small time penalty. This directly tests whether 6 min can still achieve full resolution at the lower temperature.

We have full resolution with margin and the last peak is well inside 10 min, so now trim the high-organic end to better match the actual elution window while keeping the successful 6 min, 50 C conditions. This checks whether a narrower gradient window can preserve resolution and potentially define a more efficient focused method.

The limiting pair is still 1/2, and lowering phi0 should increase their retention and spacing without sacrificing the fast 6 min method. This tests whether we can gain a bit more robustness on the critical early pair while keeping the run comfortably under 10 min.

Now that lowering phi0 improved the critical 1/2 pair, test whether the gradient can be shortened further from 6 to 4 min while preserving full resolution. This is the next logical speed optimization because all peaks are still well within 10 min and pair 1/2 has useful margin.

The 4 min method still has full resolution, so push to the shortest allowed gradient to find the speed limit. Pair 1/2 remains the constraint, and this run will show whether full resolution survives at maximum steepness or whether 4 min is the practical minimum.

Since 2 min was too steep and the earliest pair is limiting, lower phi0 one step from the successful 4 min method to give peaks 1/2 more retention and robustness while keeping the fast 4 min gradient. This explores whether 4 min can be made more selective at the front without sacrificing overall speed.

Use the robust 4 min, low-phi0 method and raise temperature to see whether we can shorten retention further while staying above 1.5 for the critical 1/2 pair. This is a direct boundary test around a known fully resolved fast method.

At 55 C the only issue is the first pair, so lowering phi0 one more step should restore early-pair resolution while keeping the faster, hotter 4 min method. This tests whether the added low-organic retention can recover R(1,2) above 1.5 without losing the short run time.

The 4 min, 50 C methods already give CRF 1.0, so now probe whether a slightly higher phi1 can further compact the late part of the run without hurting the early critical pair. This is a small focused perturbation around a proven fast method to map robustness on the high-organic end.

The slight increase to phi1 improved speed while preserving full resolution, so step phi1 up once more to see whether the late peaks can be compressed further without dropping the early limiting pair below 1.5. This is a controlled edge search around the current fastest fully resolved method.

Phi1 = 0.75 is still fully resolved but the limiting pair 1/2 is getting closer to the threshold, so take one more step upward to locate the boundary. This will tell us whether 0.75 is near-optimal or whether still faster late elution is possible at unchanged tG and T.

Since phi1 = 0.80 was too aggressive only because of pair 1/2, lower phi0 one step while keeping phi1 = 0.75 to see if extra early retention restores margin on the critical pair without giving back much speed. This tests whether we can keep the faster high-end compression and improve robustness at the front.

At phi1 = 0.75 the limiting pair is right at the threshold, so move phi0 upward one step from 0.10 to 0.15 to test whether that particular window gives a slightly better early-pair selectivity than the 0.10 or 0.05 settings. This is a fine selectivity probe around the current fastest fully resolved condition.

The 0.15–0.75 window preserved full resolution with the same speed as 0.10–0.75, so test one more increase in phi1 from this more favorable phi0 setting. This checks whether the slightly better front-end selectivity at phi0 = 0.15 allows a still faster high-organic finish without losing pair 1/2.

The fastest fully resolved region appears near phi1 = 0.75 with pair 1/2 on the boundary, so test phi0 = 0.20 to map whether a slightly higher starting strength gives a local selectivity optimum for that pair. This is a final fine-tuning check around the best short-window conditions.

The 2 min run failed only for the front pair at the narrower 0.15–0.65 window, so widening the window upward to 0.70 may ease the effective steepness enough to recover pair 1/2 while keeping the shortest gradient. This directly tests whether any 2 min method can still reach full resolution.

We have already identified 4 min methods that score 1.0, so this run is aimed at robustness benchmarking rather than score improvement: lengthening tG at the current fast window should show how much extra cushion the critical 1/2 pair gains. That helps confirm 0.10–0.75 is a stable operating region if a more conservative method is desired.

This fills in the remaining promising 4 min, 50 C window between the tested 0.05/0.75 and 0.10/0.70 conditions. It should clarify whether a slightly lower phi0 combined with a slightly lower phi1 gives a better balance for the critical 1/2 pair while staying in the fastest fully resolved region.

The boundary at high phi1 has only been explored for phi0 values 0.10 and 0.15; trying 0.05 with phi1 = 0.80 checks whether stronger early retention can keep pair 1/2 resolved while giving the shortest 4 min run in this family. With only a few injections left, this is a focused edge test around the current fastest 1.0 region.

This is the remaining untested 4 min, 50 C point between the robust 0.20–0.65 and the boundary-like 0.20–0.75 conditions, so it cleanly maps whether phi1 = 0.70 is still fully resolved at the highest phi0. With two injections left, it helps complete the local optimum surface around the fast 4 min methods.

The best fast 4 min methods at 50 C all sit close to the resolution limit for pair 1/2; dropping temperature one step should increase selectivity margin while likely keeping the already very short run well under 10 min. This final shot tests whether the same fastest window can be made more robust without sacrificing the maximum CRF.
